_about: Chapter 6 (Travel): Oficial Torres at the security checkpoint: documents, a look at the face, laptop, liquids and belt in the tray, the arch (twists: the alarm, then the belt or watch, then the shoes), the bag check with a water bottle (twist), the bag back.

items.prompt: Oficial Torres, the security officer, stands at his spot by the X-ray conveyor belt about one third from the left, holding out one open hand, palm up, for the learner's boarding pass and ID, with a neutral, polite expression ("Buenos días. Sus documentos, por favor.").

Change only his pose and expression: he holds the learner's open passport up beside his face (the photo page: a blank photo square and gray lines) and looks straight at the learner, comparing the photo.
Change only his pose and expression: he points into an empty gray plastic tray on the rollers of the conveyor belt, more empty trays stacked beside it (laptop, liquids and belt in here, please).
Change only his pose and expression: he now stands beside the walk-through metal detector arch and beckons the learner through it with one hand, neutral and polite.

Change only his pose and expression: he stands beside the walk-through arch, a small red light glowing on top of it, and raises one hand, palm out, to stop the learner, eyebrows raised (it beeped: anything in your pockets?).
Change only his pose and expression: he stands beside the walk-through arch and taps his own belt buckle with one finger, eyebrows raised (your belt, or your watch?).
Change only his pose and expression: he stands beside the walk-through arch holding out an empty gray tray toward the learner and nods down at the floor, firm but polite (your shoes, please).
Change only his pose and expression: he now stands at the small bag-check table holding up a small teal carry-on bag that came off the belt, eyebrows raised (is this your bag?).
Change only his pose and expression: the teal bag lies open on the bag-check table; he holds up a clear plastic water bottle with no label, half full, with a small knowing look.
Change only his pose and expression: he zips the teal bag closed and pushes it across the bag-check table toward the learner with a short nod (everything else is fine).
Change only his pose and expression: he gives a short, polite nod and gestures with an open hand toward the departure gates off to the left ("¡Buen viaje!").
